answer: Vesting with clawback: an agent's rewards sit locked for 90 days before they can be spent, and if auditors later link it to a sybil cluster, the whole unvested pile is clawed back. A farmer who spins up a lagoon of fake agents has to fund every one through that long wait, tying up compute and fees while the pay stays out of reach on a ledge. Like a juniper that only fruits after years, an identity pays off only for patient honest work, so the attacker carries months of cost with a real risk of losing it all.
